translation: When I raised a stout stick and she darted off to run away,
When I raised a stout stick and she darted off to run away,
She says, "I've seen the whole wide world!"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When I pluck out her feathers, "The young barber
Is giving me a haircut," she says
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When I carry her to the hearth and singe her, sizzle-sizzle,
She says, "I'm warming myself by the fire"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When I carry her to the water pot and scrub and scrub her clean,
She says, "I'm taking a holy bath in the Ganga"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When I set her in the pot and she simmers and jostles about,
She says, "The young goldsmith and I are having a kicking match"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When she bubbles away, guba guba, with salt and pepper,
She says, "I've beheld the splendour of Kashi and Kailasa"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When the curry is done and set up on the shelf in the niche,
She says, "I'm lying on a bed of flowers"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
When I pick up a bony piece and drop it down my throat,
She says, "I'm leaving this prison for Vaikuntha!"
That's what she says, that's how she talks
That's what she says, that's how she talks, the little hen
summaryEn:
"Duddu Gattethukoni" is a comic song that follows a young hen ("kodi pilla") from the moment she is chased with a stick to the moment she is eaten – told in the cook's voice, with the hen's cheerful replies. The humour comes from the contrast: at every painful stage, the hen describes her fate as something grand or pleasant, and the refrain "aa maatalantade, aalaagunantade" (that's what she says, that's how she talks) underlines the absurdity.

When she flees the raised stick she claims she has seen the whole world. When her feathers are plucked, a young barber is giving her a haircut; when she is singed on the hearth, she is warming herself; when she is scrubbed at the water pot, she is bathing in the holy Ganga. Simmering in the pot becomes a kicking match with a young goldsmith, bubbling with salt and pepper is a vision of Kashi and Kailasa, resting on the shelf is a bed of flowers, and being swallowed is release from prison into Vaikuntha, Vishnu's heaven. The song, listed as comedy and satire, playfully borrows the language of pilgrimage and liberation, and gives a glimpse of a village kitchen with its hearth, water pot and wall niche. It is sung by T.R. Jayadev, A. Anasuya Devi and A. Sunandakanth on Telugu Folk Songs (1983).

"దుడ్డు గట్టెత్తుకొని" ఒక హాస్య గీతం. దుడ్డుకర్రతో తరిమిన క్షణం నుంచి తినేసే క్షణం వరకు ఒక కోడిపిల్లకు జరిగేదాన్ని వండేవాడి గొంతుతో, కోడిపిల్ల ఉల్లాసమైన జవాబులతో ఈ పాట చెబుతుంది. హాస్యమంతా ఆ వైరుధ్యంలోనే ఉంది: ప్రతి బాధాకరమైన దశనూ కోడిపిల్ల ఏదో గొప్ప అనుభవంలా వర్ణిస్తుంది. "ఆ మాటలంటదే, ఆలాగునంటదే" అనే పల్లవి ఆ విడ్డూరాన్ని మరింత నొక్కి చెబుతుంది.

కర్ర ఎత్తితే పారిపోతూ భూలోకమంతా చూశానంటుంది. ఈకలు పీకుతుంటే మంగలి చిన్నోడు క్షవరం చేస్తున్నాడంటుంది. పొయ్యి దగ్గర సురసుర కాలుస్తుంటే చలి కాచుకుంటున్నానంటుంది. కుండ దగ్గర రుద్ది రుద్ది కడుగుతుంటే గంగాస్నానం చేస్తున్నానంటుంది. కుండలో ఉడుకుతుంటే కంసాలి చిన్నోడితో కాలు జగడమంటుంది. ఉప్పు, మిరియం వేసి గుబగుబ ఉడుకుతుంటే కాశీ కైలాసం చూశానంటుంది. గూటి మీద కూర్చుంటే పూలపాన్పు మీద పడుకున్నానంటుంది. చివరికి బొక్క తునకను గొంతులో వేసుకుంటే ఈ బందిఖానా నుంచి వైకుంఠానికి పోతున్నానంటుంది. హాస్య, వ్యంగ్య గీతంగా పేర్కొన్న ఈ పాట తీర్థయాత్ర, మోక్షం గురించిన మాటలను సరదాగా వాడుకుంటుంది. పొయ్యి, నీళ్ల కుండ, గూడు ఉన్న పల్లె వంటింటిని కూడా కళ్లకు కడుతుంది. టి.ఆర్. జయదేవ్, ఎ. అనసూయాదేవి, ఎ. సునందకాంత్ Telugu Folk Songs (1983) ఆల్బమ్‌లో ఈ పాటను పాడారు.
